newsitem.title: USA: First US corporate junk bonds of week to hit mart.
newsitem.headline: First US corporate junk bonds of week to hit mart.

text.p: Ameriserve Food Distribution Inc's $500 million junk bond offering is likely to price Wednesday morning, kicking off this week's busy schedule of large high-yield deals, syndicate officials said.
In the investment-grade market, Philip Morris Cos Inc will grab the spotlight by launching a $1.0 billion offering of eight-year debt via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Ameriserve will use proceeds from its offering to finance the purchase of PepsiCo Inc's PFS restaurant supply distribution unit.
The acquisition will make AmeriServe the largest systems foodservice distributor in North America.
Price talk on the $500 million AmeriServe 10-year senior subordinated notes is 9-3/4-10 percent.
Nebco Evans Holding Co, the parent company of AmeriServe, will simutaneously price $50 million in 10-year senior discount notes. Price talk is 225 basis points over the yield on the AmeriServe bonds.
Both transactions will be underwriten by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.

AmeriServe's offering will be followed later in the week by two large junk bond deals: a $750 million two-part offering from Iridium LLC and a $600 million offering from Host Marriot Corp subsidiary, HMH Properties Inc.
The Iridium offering, via Chase Securities Inc, received a lift on Wednesday morning when the company successfully launched five low-earth-orbiting satellites.

While the deployment only brings the total number of orbiting satellites to 17 out of a total of 66 needed to complete the network, analysts expected it to provide a boost to the company's junk bond transaction, expected for Thursday.
